title: KCET 2013 Maths
subject: maths
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: If $\dfrac{(x+1)^2}{x^3+x}=\dfrac{A}{x}+\dfrac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}$, then $\sin^{-1}A+\tan^{-1}B+\sec^{-1}C=$
questions.explanation: Comparing coefficients gives $A=1,B=0,C=2$, so $\sin^{-1}1+\tan^{-1}0+\sec^{-1}2=\pi/2+0+\pi/3=5\pi/6$.

questions.q: The sum of the series $\dfrac{1}{2\cdot3}\cdot2+\dfrac{2}{3\cdot4}\cdot2^2+\dfrac{3}{4\cdot5}\cdot2^3+\ldots$ to n terms is
questions.explanation: The general term telescopes as $b_{k+1}-b_k$ with $b_k=\dfrac{2^k}{k+1}$, giving the sum $\dfrac{2^{n+1}}{n+2}-1$.

questions.q: If the roots of the equation $x^3+ax^2+bx+c=0$ are in A.P., then $2a^3-9ab=$
questions.explanation: The middle root equals $-a/3$; substituting into the cubic and simplifying gives $2a^3-9ab=-27c$.

questions.q: If the value of $C_0+2\cdot C_1+3\cdot C_2+\ldots+(n+1)\cdot C_n=576$, then n is
The inverse of the proposition $(p\wedge\sim q)\to r$ is
questions.explanation: Negating both the hypothesis and conclusion of $(p\wedge\sim q)\to r$ gives $(\sim p\vee q)\to\sim r$.

questions.q: The range of the function $f(x)=\sin[x]$, $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}<x<\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ where $[x]$ denotes the greatest integer $\le x$, is
questions.explanation: $[x]=0$ for $0\le x<\pi/4$ giving $\sin0=0$, and $[x]=-1$ for $-\pi/4<x<0$ giving $\sin(-1)=-\sin1$.

questions.q: If the line $6x-7y+8+\lambda(3x-y+5)=0$ is parallel to y-axis, then $\lambda=$
questions.explanation: The coefficient of y must vanish: $-7-\lambda=0\Rightarrow\lambda=-7$.

questions.q: The angle between the lines $\sin^2\alpha\cdot y^2-2xy\cos^2\alpha+(\cos^2\alpha-1)x^2=0$ is
questions.explanation: Using $\tan\theta=\dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2-ab}}{a+b}$ with $a+b=0$ here, the angle is $90°$.

questions.q: The minimum area of the triangle formed by the variable line $3\cos\theta\cdot x+4\sin\theta\cdot y=12$ and the co-ordinate axes is
questions.explanation: Area $=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{4}{\cos\theta}\cdot\dfrac{3}{\sin\theta}=\dfrac{12}{\sin2\theta}$, minimized at $\sin2\theta=1$ giving area 12.

questions.q: $\log(\sin1°)\cdot\log(\sin2°)\cdot\log(\sin3°)\ldots\log(\sin179°)$
questions.explanation: Since $\sin90°=1$, the factor $\log(\sin90°)=0$ makes the whole product zero.

questions.q: If $\sin x-\sin y=\dfrac12$ and $\cos x-\cos y=1$, then $\tan(x+y)=$
questions.explanation: Dividing the sum-to-product forms gives $\cot\dfrac{x+y}{2}=-\dfrac12$, so $\tan(x+y)=\dfrac{2(-2)}{1-4}=\dfrac43$.

questions.q: In a triangle ABC, if $\dfrac{\cos A}{a}=\dfrac{\cos B}{b}=\dfrac{\cos C}{c}$ and $a=2$, then its area is
questions.explanation: The condition forces the triangle to be equilateral, so with side 2 the area is $\sqrt3$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to0}\dfrac{\log_e(1+x)}{3^x-1}=$
questions.explanation: Using $\ln(1+x)\sim x$ and $3^x-1\sim x\ln3$, the limit is $\dfrac{1}{\ln3}=\log_3e$.

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\begin{cases}x, & x\text{ is irrational}\\0, & x\text{ is rational}\end{cases}$, then f is
questions.explanation: Near $x=0$ both rational and irrational sequences give function values approaching 0, but at any other point they give different limits, so f is continuous only at $x=0$.

questions.q: In a regular graph of 15 vertices the sum of the degree of the vertices is 60. Then the degree of each vertex is
questions.explanation: In a regular graph, sum of degrees $=n\cdot d=15d=60\Rightarrow d=4$.

questions.q: The remainder when $10^{10}\cdot(10^{10}+1)(10^{10}+2)$ is divided by 6 is
questions.explanation: $10^{10}\equiv4\pmod6$, so the three factors are $\equiv4,5,0\pmod6$; since one factor is divisible by 6, the product's remainder is 0.

questions.q: A value of x satisfying $150x\equiv35\pmod{31}$ is
questions.explanation: Reducing gives $26x\equiv4\pmod{31}$; since $5^{-1}\equiv25\pmod{31}$, solving yields $x\equiv24\pmod{31}$.

questions.q: The smallest positive divisor greater than 1 of a composite number 'a' is
questions.explanation: If the smallest prime factor exceeded $\sqrt a$, all its factors would exceed $\sqrt a$, making the product exceed a; hence it is $\le\sqrt a$.

questions.q: If A and B are square matrices of order 'n' such that $A^2-B^2=(A-B)(A+B)$, then which of the following will be true?
options: Either of A or B is zero matrix.
Either of A or B is an identity matrix.
questions.explanation: Expanding $(A-B)(A+B)=A^2+AB-BA-B^2$ and equating to $A^2-B^2$ gives $AB=BA$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}\alpha&2\\2&\alpha\end{bmatrix}$ and $|A^3|=125$, then $\alpha=$
questions.explanation: $|A|^3=(\alpha^2-4)^3=125\Rightarrow\alpha^2-4=5\Rightarrow\alpha=\pm3$.

questions.q: If $A=\begin{vmatrix}x&1&1\\1&x&1\\1&1&x\end{vmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{vmatrix}x&1\\1&x\end{vmatrix}$, then $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=$
If the determinant of the adjoint of a (real) matrix of order 3 is 25, then the determinant of the inverse of the matrix is
If the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}2&3\\5&-1\end{bmatrix}=A+B$, where A is symmetric and B is skew symmetric, then $B=$
questions.explanation: $B=\dfrac{M-M^T}{2}=\dfrac12\begin{bmatrix}0&-2\\2&0\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{bmatrix}$.

questions.q: In a group (G, *), for some element 'a' of G, if $a^2=e$, where e is the identity element, then
questions.explanation: $a^2=e\Rightarrow a\cdot a=e\Rightarrow a=a^{-1}$.

questions.q: In the group (Z, *), if $a*b=a+b-n$ for all $a,b\in Z$, where n is a fixed integer, then the inverse of $(-n)$ is
questions.explanation: The identity element is n; solving $(-n)*b=n$ gives $-n+b-n=n\Rightarrow b=3n$.

questions.q: If $\vec a=(1,2,3)$, $\vec b=(2,-1,1)$, $\vec c=(3,2,1)$ and $\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=\alpha\vec a+\beta\vec b+\gamma\vec c$, then
questions.explanation: By $\vec a\times(\vec b\times\vec c)=\vec b(\vec a\cdot\vec c)-\vec c(\vec a\cdot\vec b)=10\vec b-3\vec c$, giving $\alpha=0,\beta=10,\gamma=-3$ (KEA awarded a grace mark for this question).

questions.q: If $\vec a\perp\vec b$ and $(\vec a+\vec b)\perp(\vec a+m\vec b)$, then $m=$
questions.explanation: Expanding the dot product using $\vec a\cdot\vec b=0$ gives $|\vec a|^2+m|\vec b|^2=0\Rightarrow m=-|\vec a|^2/|\vec b|^2$.

questions.q: If $\vec a,\vec b,\vec c$ are unit vectors such that $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=\vec 0$, then $\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a=$
questions.explanation: Squaring $\vec a+\vec b+\vec c=0$ gives $3+2(\vec a\cdot\vec b+\vec b\cdot\vec c+\vec c\cdot\vec a)=0$, so the sum is $-3/2$.

questions.q: If $\vec a$ is a vector perpendicular to both $\vec b$ and $\vec c$, then
questions.explanation: Since $\vec a$ is parallel to $\vec b\times\vec c$, their cross product vanishes.

questions.q: A tangent is drawn to the circle $2x^2+2y^2-3x+4y=0$ at the point 'A' and it meets the line $x+y=3$ at $B(2,1)$, then $AB=$
questions.explanation: The tangent length from B equals $\sqrt{\text{power of }B}=\sqrt{2^2+1^2-1.5(2)+2(1)}=\sqrt4=2$.

questions.q: The area of the circle having its centre at $(3,4)$ and touching the line $5x+12y-11=0$ is
The number of real circles cutting orthogonally the circle $x^2+y^2+2x-2y+7=0$ is
questions.explanation: The orthogonality condition $2g_1g_2+2f_1f_2=c_1+c_2$ is a single linear relation in the unknown circle's coefficients, satisfied by infinitely many real circles even though the given circle itself is imaginary (radius$^2<0$); KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The length of the chord of the circle $x^2+y^2+3x+2y-8=0$ intercepted by the y-axis is
questions.explanation: Setting $x=0$ gives $y^2+2y-8=0\Rightarrow y=2,-4$, so the chord length is 6.

questions.q: $A\equiv(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, $B\equiv(\sin\theta,-\cos\theta)$ are two points. The locus of the centroid of $\triangle OAB$, where 'O' is the origin, is
questions.explanation: The centroid is $\left(\dfrac{\cos\theta+\sin\theta}{3},\dfrac{\sin\theta-\cos\theta}{3}\right)$, so $x^2+y^2=\dfrac29$, i.e. $9x^2+9y^2=2$.

questions.q: The sum of the squares of the eccentricities of the conics $\dfrac{x^2}{4}+\dfrac{y^2}{3}=1$ and $\dfrac{x^2}{4}-\dfrac{y^2}{3}=1$ is
questions.explanation: For the ellipse $e^2=1-3/4=1/4$ and for the hyperbola $e^2=1+3/4=7/4$; their sum is 2.

questions.q: The equation of the tangent to the parabola $y^2=4x$ inclined at an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to the +ve direction of x-axis is
questions.explanation: Using $y=mx+1/m$ with $m=1$ (since $4a=4\Rightarrow a=1$) gives $y=x+1$, i.e. $x-y+1=0$.

questions.q: If the distance between the foci and the distance between the directrices of the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ are in the ratio 3 : 2, then $a:b$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{2ae}{2a/e}=e^2=\dfrac32\Rightarrow b^2/a^2=1/2\Rightarrow a:b=\sqrt2:1$.

questions.q: If the area of the auxiliary circle of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}+\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ $(a>b)$ is twice the area of the ellipse, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.explanation: $\pi a^2=2\pi ab\Rightarrow a=2b$, so $e^2=1-b^2/a^2=3/4\Rightarrow e=\sqrt3/2$.

questions.q: $\cos\left[2\cos^{-1}\dfrac15+\sin^{-1}\dfrac15\right]=$
questions.explanation: Writing the angle as $\cos^{-1}(1/5)+\pi/2$, the cosine becomes $-\sin(\cos^{-1}(1/5))=-2\sqrt6/5$.

questions.q: The value of $\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-y}{x+y}\right)$, $x,y>0$ is
questions.explanation: This is a standard identity: $\tan^{-1}(x/y)-\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x-y}{x+y}\right)=\pi/4$ for $x,y>0$.

questions.q: The general solution of $\sin x-\cos x=\sqrt2$, for any integer 'n' is
questions.explanation: $\sqrt2\sin(x-\pi/4)=\sqrt2\Rightarrow\sin(x-\pi/4)=1\Rightarrow x=2n\pi+3\pi/4$.

questions.q: The modulus and amplitude of $\dfrac{1+2i}{1-(1-i)^2}$ are
questions.explanation: $(1-i)^2=-2i$, so the expression is $\dfrac{1+2i}{1+2i}=1$, with modulus 1 and amplitude 0.

questions.q: If $2x=-1+\sqrt3i$, then the value of $(1-x^2+x)^6-(1-x+x^2)^6=$
questions.explanation: Here $x$ is a complex cube root of unity satisfying $x^2+x+1=0$; both bracketed expressions reduce to $\mp2x^2,-2x$ whose sixth powers use $x^6=1$, giving the difference 0.

questions.q: If $x+y=\tan^{-1}y$ and $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=f(y)\dfrac{dy}{dx}$, then $f(y)=$
questions.explanation: Differentiating gives $dy/dx=-(1+y^2)/y^2$; differentiating again shows $f(y)=2/y^3$.

questions.q: $f(x)=\begin{cases}2a-x, & -a<x<a\\3x-2a, & a\le x\end{cases}$. Then which of the following is true?
questions.explanation: The function is continuous at $x=a$ (both pieces equal $a$), but the left derivative $-1$ differs from the right derivative $3$.

questions.q: Let $f(x)=\cos^{-1}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{13}}(2\cos x-3\sin x)\right]$. Then $f'(0.5)=$
questions.explanation: Writing $2\cos x-3\sin x=\sqrt{13}\cos(x+\phi)$ gives $f(x)=x+\phi$, so $f'(x)=1$ everywhere.

questions.q: If $f(x)$ is a function such that $f''(x)+f(x)=0$ and $g(x)=[f(x)]^2+[f'(x)]^2$ and $g(3)=8$, then $g(8)=$
questions.explanation: $g'(x)=2f'(x)[f(x)+f''(x)]=0$, so g is constant; hence $g(8)=g(3)=8$.

questions.q: If $f(x)=f'(x)+f''(x)+f'''(x)+\ldots$ and $f(0)=1$, then $f(x)=$
questions.explanation: Differentiating shows $f'(x)=f(x)-f'(x)$, so $2f'=f$, giving $f(x)=e^{x/2}$ since $f(0)=1$.

questions.q: The function $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{3}+\dfrac{3}{x}$ decreases in the interval
questions.explanation: $f'(x)=\dfrac13-\dfrac{3}{x^2}<0\Rightarrow x^2<9\Rightarrow -3<x<3$.

questions.q: If $\sin^{-1}a$ is the acute angle between the curves $x^2+y^2=4x$ and $x^2+y^2=8$ at $(2,2)$, then $a=$
questions.explanation: The tangent slopes at $(2,2)$ are 0 and $-1$, so $\tan\theta=1\Rightarrow\theta=45°$, giving $a=\sin45°=1/\sqrt2$.

questions.q: The maximum area of a rectangle that can be inscribed in a circle of radius 2 units is
questions.explanation: The maximum-area rectangle is a square with diagonal 4, giving side $2\sqrt2$ and area 8.

questions.q: If the length of the sub-tangent at any point to the curve $xy^n=a$ is proportional to the abscissa, then 'n' is
questions.explanation: The subtangent is $y/y'=-nx$, which is proportional to the abscissa x for any value of n.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\cos^{n-1}x}{\sin^{n+1}x}\,dx$, $n\ne0$ is
questions.explanation: Writing the integrand as $\cot^{n-1}x\csc^2x$ and substituting $u=\cot x$ gives $-\dfrac{\cot^nx}{n}+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int\dfrac{(x-1)e^x}{(x+1)^3}\,dx=$
questions.explanation: With $f(x)=1/(x+1)^2$, $f(x)+f'(x)=(x-1)/(x+1)^3$, so by $\int e^x[f+f']dx=e^xf(x)$ the integral is $e^x/(x+1)^2$.

questions.q: If $I_1=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}x\cdot\sin x\,dx$ and $I_2=\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}x\cdot\cos x\,dx$, then which one of the following is true?
questions.explanation: Integration by parts gives $I_1=1$ and $I_2=\pi/2-1$, so $I_1+I_2=\pi/2$.

questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2}\dfrac{|x|}{x}\,dx$ is
$\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi}\dfrac{\cos^4x}{\cos^4x+\sin^4x}\,dx=$
questions.explanation: On $[0,\pi/2]$, $\int\cos^4/(\cos^4+\sin^4)\,dx+\int\sin^4/(\cos^4+\sin^4)\,dx=\pi/2$, and by symmetry the two are equal, so each is $\pi/4$; by $f(\pi-x)=f(x)$ the integral over $[\pi/2,\pi]$ repeats this, giving a total of $\pi/2$.

questions.q: The area bounded by the curve $y=\sin\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)$, x-axis and lines $x=0$ and $x=3\pi$ is
questions.explanation: Over $[0,3\pi]$, $x/3$ ranges over $[0,\pi]$ where sine is non-negative, so area $=\int_0^{3\pi}\sin(x/3)\,dx=6$.

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\sqrt{1-x^2y^2}\cdot dx=y\cdot dx+x\cdot dy$ is
questions.explanation: Since $y\,dx+x\,dy=d(xy)$, the equation becomes $\sqrt{1-u^2}\,dx=du$ with $u=xy$, integrating to $u=\sin(x+c)$, i.e. $\sin(x+c)=xy$.

questions.q: If 'm' and 'n' are the order and degree of the differential equation $(y'')^5+4\cdot\dfrac{(y'')^3}{y'''}+y'''=\sin x$, then
questions.explanation: Clearing the fraction by multiplying through by $y'''$ gives $(y'')^5y'''+4(y'')^3+(y''')^2=y'''\sin x$, a polynomial equation of order 3 (highest derivative $y'''$) and degree 2.
